name: Portfolio
action: 18 of the 30 most similar days were followed by a rise (average -0.01%); usual rate 56% over 251 days; worked out on earlier weights, because too few of the present holdings have a year of stored prices
plan: The 10-year yield is still 5.24%, up 28bp in a month, and the Fed raised rates in September. Wednesday's CPI is forecast to rise to 3.6% from 3.4%, so buyers have little reason to add risk before it. Consumer sentiment fell again to 46.3, Thursday's AI sell-off (OpenAI revenue below expectations) has not been repaired, and with the bond market shut on Monday for Columbus Day trading will be thin. The S&P 500 is already 1.4% above its 20-day average.
lesson: No adjustment. The similar-day evidence is flat and the news is balanced: this is close to a coin flip, a shade below the usual rate.
text: Friday's rally had breadth: the Dow rose 0.8% and the S&P 500 0.6% to end the week up about 1%, led by healthcare and property. Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the 3 November midterms, and Iran is reviewing a US reply on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, so the oil fear premium is easing. The 10-year yield is 4bp lower over five sessions and results season opens on Tuesday with the banks.

plan: The same weekend news is bad for the index: oil above $104 with talks stalled feeds an inflation number that is already forecast at 0.6% on the month on Wednesday, and the Fed raised rates in September. The US bond market is shut on Monday, so shares trade without a yield signal and volume will be thin. Chip stocks faded from their opens on both Thursday and Friday after the OpenAI revenue report, and 20% of the portfolio is in them. An oil gap at the open may fade through the session, as weekend markets barely moved.
lesson: Weekend news (Hormuz talks stalled, confirmed tanker strikes) points to firmer oil, a small negative for the index and a small positive for a portfolio that is 40% oil majors.
text: Shares ended last week firm: the S&P 500 rose 0.6% on Friday and about 1.2% on the week, set a record on the way, and breadth was roughly two to one positive. TSMC has already reported third-quarter revenue above its own guidance, and results season opens on Tuesday with banks expected to show strong trading income. The 10-year yield fell 4bp on the week after a well-received auction. For this portfolio the weekend helps: Iran called the US reply on Hormuz insufficient and tanker attacks were confirmed, which supports the 40% in oil majors.

plan: CPI lands at 13:30 UK before the US open, with headline forecasts as high as 0.6% on the month and August's core at 0.3%; a hot print would push the 10-year back towards 5.31% and hit software and chips, about 35% of this portfolio. The portfolio is light on AI, the weakest group, and its new health care weight sits on the side of the rotation. Low yield moves have historically been followed by up days for this portfolio.
